document_note: L8-2DV reconciled evidence. Section original_l82d_evidence is the unmodified L8-2D document; every other section is new and separately identified.

original_l82d_evidence.scope: Operational behavior of the committed Level 8 service under constrained concurrent workloads, and flat-image compatibility. Engineering evidence from one host; not a production SLO, not model validity, not a hard network response-time guarantee.
failed_gates: P2_r3: offered prediction workload valid (no missed arrivals, scheduling-lag p99 <= 5 ms)
P2_r3: prediction p95 degradation vs matched P0_r3

host_and_docker_vm.docker: Docker Desktop 29.5.3, Linux VM kernel 6.12.76-linuxkit, cgroup v2
host_and_docker_vm.other_load: two unrelated PostgreSQL containers present (one running, idle and healthy; one exited)

server_container.image: flat-layout image derived from running-readiness-level7:4.0.0 + the ten hash-locked Level 8 wheels + the committed F1 Level 7 service + the committed Level 8 modules
server_container.instrumented_variant_image_id: sha256:67924bcdc3ec (adds one scratch wrapper module with a polled /__bench/diag route; used for P4 and P5 only)
server_container.torch_configuration: unchanged: parent default; child 1 intra-op and 1 inter-op thread

environment.network: isolated internal Docker network (no external access, no published host ports)
environment.cpu_isolation_caveat: A CPU quota limits CPU time, it does not give dedicated cores: server and generator share a 4-core/8-thread host (and the Docker VM) with each other and with whatever else runs on it.
environment.monitoring_overhead: cgroup/proc sampling by docker exec every 5 s (a short shell process inside the server container); instrumented runs additionally poll one diagnostics route at 1 Hz. The unmodified-application runs (P0-P3) have no per-request instrumentation.

methodology.profiles: P0 predict 100/s open-loop; P1 +4 closed-loop explanation callers; P2 +40/s open-loop explanations; P3 four closed-loop explanation callers only; P4 100/s predict + one synchronized burst of 32 explanations at +1 s of a 10 s window (after 10 s warm-up); P5 five-minute soak with four callers (after 10 s warm-up)
methodology.windows: P0-P3: 10 s warm-up + 30 s measurement; three matched repetitions of P0-P2 in a balanced cyclic order; P4 three times; P5 once
methodology.server_lifecycle_per_run: fresh container per run; readiness = health 200 and first successful explanation; resource sample; load; 3 s drain; resource sample; docker stop (15 s grace); exit code, OOM flag and logs recorded
methodology.latency_definitions: request = actual start to completion; scheduled = scheduled arrival to completion (open-loop only); all-completed includes non-200 responses; successful = 200 with a valid, associated payload
methodology.degradation_gate: mixed prediction p95 minus matched P0 p95 <= max(20% of baseline, 5 ms); P4/P5 use the median of the three P0 repetitions
methodology.generator_validity: offered workload considered valid when no arrival is missed and scheduling-lag p99 <= 5 ms; generator CPU and event-loop lag are recorded to separate generator saturation from server saturation
methodology.instrumented_vs_unmodified: P0-P3 measure the unmodified committed application; P4 and P5 use a wrapper that adds one polled diagnostics route (needed for dispatcher high-water marks) and are compared with the unmodified P0 baseline
methodology.failure_policy: no run was discarded or selected; one supplementary repetition of P2 was added after an anomaly and is reported separately

workload_inputs.composition: 40 development-range draws + 10 near-threshold draws (smallest |logit| of a 20,000-point development-range pool)
workload_inputs.construction: numpy.random.default_rng(42) via tests/level8_oracle.build_grids; synthetic; no holdout, no health data
workload_inputs.expected_results: prediction probability/decision per input computed once from the repository-layout Level 7 runtime and embedded in the load generator
workload_inputs.request_result_association: every response is checked against the expected result for the exact input that was sent

P2_r4_supplementary.why: one extra P2 repetition after the P2_r3 anomaly, to test reproducibility; not a replacement for any run

incident_P2_r3.interpretation: An explanation exceeded its execution deadline once (one 504), the dispatcher replaced the worker, explanations were unavailable for the replacement's startup, and /predict stalled for about two seconds while the replacement started. Generator CPU was far below its quota, so the stall is attributed to the server side. The trigger of the deadline event was not established and the event did not recur in 12 other runs or the supplementary repetition. A contention between the replacement's start-up and the parent for the 4-CPU quota is consistent with the throttling and stall but is NOT proven.
incident_P2_r3.treatment: reported as measured; the run is part of the prescribed three repetitions and its gates fail; it was not repeated to replace it

predict.reported_scheduled_in_window_field_actua: attempted arrivals (it is derived from the scheduling-lag list, which only records issued requests)

findings: Prediction: 4,000 scheduled arrivals over the 40 s run, 3,642 attempted, 358 missed. All 358 misses fall in the measurement window (none in warm-up), derived independently from schedule gaps and equal to the generator's counter.

The summary field scheduled_in_window actually counts attempted requests (it is derived from the scheduling-lag list, which only contains issued requests). The true scheduled number in the window is 3,000. This is a reporting defect: success over scheduled arrivals (0.881) is not what the field implies. No measurement is wrong.

Latency percentiles are measured from just before client.post to completion, so they include connection acquisition, request transmission, response body and JSON parsing; they exclude the scheduling delay (reported separately) and the response validation, which happens after the end timestamp.
Scheduled-arrival latency covers only issued requests: missed arrivals are excluded, so it understates user-visible latency when arrivals are missed (survivorship).

The 2 s client timeout is an httpx per-phase timeout (connect, write, read, pool), not a total deadline: 144 prediction requests took 2.0 s or more and the longest took 7.8 s with zero client timeouts. The longest requests were issued while the server and the generator loop were both stalled; their latency includes waiting for pool slots (maximum in-flight predictions reached 143, above the 128-connection limit, because the backlog check counts a request only once its task starts).
Outstanding requests at window end: zero (the generator drains all tasks before summarizing).
No accounting defect changes a conclusion: the P2 repetition 3 failure and the stall are real; the missed-arrival count is correct.
defects_requiring_a_separate_source_appr: rename or correct the scheduled_in_window summary field
count in-flight requests at task creation so the backlog bound cannot exceed the connection limit

confirmed_findings: The original L8-2D result is FAIL and remains FAIL. All five failures belong to P2 repetition 3; every other primary run met its gates as originally reported.

Gate reconciliation: the L8-2D thread and shutdown criteria had been replaced after measurement. Under the reviewed accounting (119 gates) 104 pass, 5 fail and 10 are NOT VERIFIED; no gate that originally failed now passes.

Prediction accounting for P2 repetition 3 is internally consistent: 4,000 scheduled, 3,642 attempted, 358 missed, all in the measurement window; every attempted prediction returned 200. The scheduled_in_window summary field actually counts attempted requests.
The 2 s client timeout is per-phase, not a total deadline; 144 predictions took at least 2.0 s (longest 7.8 s) without a client timeout.

The original stall: explanation throughput fell from about 30 s into the run, prediction completions collapsed for about 5.5 s from 30.5 s, the first 504 came at about 32 s, explanations were unavailable from about 33 s to 38.9 s, and traffic recovered by about 39-40 s. An earlier, smaller blip (a few overloaded responses and one 442 ms bucket) occurred at about 11 s.

Controlled recovery (two repetitions): after SIGKILL of only the worker, the dispatcher noticed within 0.1 s and the replacement was ready after 2.6-2.7 s, explanations were unavailable for about 2.5 s, a subsequent explanation succeeded, and cleanup was clean. Prediction stayed 100% successful with no missed arrivals; event-window p95 was 9.7 ms and 22.7 ms (no-fault baseline at the same offsets: about 10 ms) and the largest single latency was 70 ms and 87 ms. Container CPU rose to about 1.5 cores with two throttle periods (415 ms and 687 ms throttled), without a stall comparable to the original 2-7 s.
Three targeted P2 reproductions did not reproduce the anomaly (NOT REPRODUCED): no restart, no non-200 explanation, no missed arrival, prediction p95 6.5-9.9 ms, explanation p95 28.9-32.8 ms.

Thread retention behaves as the installed anyio implementation predicts: idle request-pool workers are retained and pruned lazily on the next pool call. In the pre-registered test parent threads stayed constant during a 16.4 s idle drain, fell to baseline within 2 s of one /health call, and a second load cycle peaked at the same count; child threads and file descriptors were stable. No leak was found.
unresolved_hypotheses: Trigger of the original execution-deadline event: not established; no dispatcher counter or log existed in the unmodified run.

Host-level disturbance as a common cause of the server and generator stalls: consistent with the timing (host file-access waves at 16:13:03-16:13:25 overlap the stall at 16:13:11-16:13:21; the generator loop itself lagged 561 ms at low CPU) but correlation only; no host log was available.

Worker-replacement CPU contention as the cause of the 2 s prediction stall: NOT supported by the isolated recovery tests (prediction was nearly unaffected) although the mixed-load case (replacement during 40 explanations/s) was not tested.
Holdout metadata discrepancy: responsible process unidentified; holdout_non_access NOT VERIFIED.
